segments: "for
that region of Jerusalem
is a thirsty land,
and behold, the Arabs have ruined all the water that was around it,
and the river is more than a parasang distant.
And do not think
that Jerusalem is like Acre.
Believe [me],
were it not for the sea,
we would not have been able to sit against Acre for two days."
And they all listened to his counsel,
and marched toward Gaza.
Now Saladin, even though he was glad that they turned their gaze away from Jerusalem,
yet feared for Egypt.
And then the king sent an envoy to Saladin, saying to him:
"Do not think that from fear or weakness I have withdrawn.
For the ram of the sheep does not back up
except to strike the head.
Therefore, if you make peace in what we desire,
it is good for you;
behold, I have informed you."
And after many embassies, peace was made:
that the places which were with the Franks should belong to the Franks,
namely Jaffa and its territory, Caesarea, Arsuf, Haifa, Acre, Antioch, and Tripoli;
and the rest of the places to the Arabs;
and that Ashkelon should be desolate.
And Saladin gave the Franks the amount of gold that they had spent on the rebuilding of Ashkelon.
And the way was opened, and a multitude of Franks came and worshipped in Jerusalem;
and Saladin honored all of them,
and gave gifts and mounts.
And it is said
that the King of England sent and said to Saladin:
"Whosoever does not have with him a token from me among the Franks,
do not allow him to enter Jerusalem."
And Saladin gathered his wise men and asked them:
"What is the king's purpose in this?" And having reflected, they answered him:
"The great reason for the setting out of the Franks is nothing else
than worship in Jerusalem.
And when this happens for them,
and they return to their country,
they will not want to set out again.
And on this account the king is holding them back,
so that another time when he wishes to set out, they will set out with him willingly and zealously."
And when Saladin understood this, he sent word to the king:
"These men are strangers,
and after the peace, I am not able to distress them.
If you restrain them,
you are able [to do so]."
